text.p: Italian debt instruments closed weaker after France's new Socialist-led government called for a "period of reflection" on the single European currency budget stability pact.

"The possibility of EMU-linked problems has become a certainty and the market is reacting as a consequence," one trader said, adding there had been a wave of systematic but not overwhelming selling pressure which came up against few buyers.
The September Liffe Btp contract ended near support levels at 129.50 after touching an afternoon low at 129.25. In cash bonds, the Feb 2007 was 56 basis points off at 96.96.

The September Btp had attempted to rise at the start in the wake of positive bunds and following a brilliant performance in Treasuries on Friday. But news began trickling through from the Luxembourg Ecofin meeting, inciting operators to caution.

"Fears of an EMU delay are benefiting the mark, while the dollar is weaker, and while bunds and French bonds are consolidating," one trader said, noting tensions continued to hit the high yielders, Italian Btps particularly.
"Until we get clarification of the French attitude to EMU we will have to just get used to going up and down, moving on technical factors," another operator said.
Traders said a first indication of the French view could come on Thursday from a Jospin-Santer meeting on the stability pact.
The 10-year spread over benchmark bunds widened to 152 basis points from 141 at Friday's close.
